brief: a tense job interview scene where the candidate realises the interviewer is her ex
concept: Two people pretending to be strangers, and the camera that refuses to let them.
plan_outline: 1. WS · eye · static · glass meeting room, cool office light · a candidate sits; the interviewer's chair is empty (5 s)
2. MS · eye · static · same room · a man in his thirties enters, sits, opens a folder, then looks up (4 s)
3. CU · eye · push in · same room · the candidate's face as she recognises him (4 s)
4. OTS · eye · static · same room, over her shoulder · he holds the look a beat too long, then smiles politely (4 s)
5. OTS · eye · static · reverse, over his shoulder · she smiles back, too brightly (4 s)
6. ECU · eye · static · the table · his pen stops writing (3 s)
7. WS · high · static · same room · the two of them, small, the city behind the glass (5 s)
why: OTS pairs keep the 180° rule and make the power exchange readable.
The push-in is reserved for the moment of recognition; everything else is still — tension through restraint.
The insert (the pen stopping) tells us he is shaken without a line of dialogue.
A high wide at the end makes them small inside the cold glass room: the subtext in one frame.
